summary: A 1945 Arkansas Forestry Commission lookout in Newton County: an 85-foot Aermotor now privately owned by Ed Porter, whose restored ground house is a rental.

facts.design: Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot metal cab

access.note: Tower and land are privately owned by Ed Porter; the sources do not say whether the tower is open to climb.

events.note: Built by the Arkansas Forestry Commission; 85-foot Aermotor

evidence.supports: built 1945 by the Arkansas Forestry Commission; 85-foot Aermotor with 7x7 metal cab
evidence.quote: This 85' Aermotor tower with 7'x7' metal cab was built in 1945 by the Arkansas Forestry Commission.

evidence.supports: 85-foot Aermotor, 7 x 7 cab, Arkansas Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: An 85-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 cab was constructed by the Arkansas Forestry Commission.
The Arkansas Forestry Commission was established by Act 234 in 1931
and it too built many more towers

evidence.supports: Ed Porter bought tower, ground house and land when surplused
evidence.quote: When surplused, Ed Porter bought the tower, ground house and land.

evidence.supports: ground house restored and offered as a lookout rental, rare in the Eastern U.S.
evidence.quote: The ground house has been restored and is available as a lookout rental site

evidence.supports: 1971 survey: owned by the State of Arkansas
evidence.quote: OWNED BY THE STATE OF ARKANSAS

evidence.supports: 1971 survey: station on property owned by Mr. Permee
evidence.quote: ON PROPERTY OWNED BY MR. PERMEE

evidence.supports: Ed Porter as nominator and owner
ground house rental, rare in the Eastern U.S.

corrections.why: The register says Ed Porter bought the tower, ground house and land after it was surplused, so the state no longer owns it. The record's state ownership is out of date.

notes_for_editor: No source beyond the NHLR confirms the Ed Porter rental or the tower's climbability; one WebSearch found nothing. The sale date to Porter is unknown. The 1971 survey places the station on land owned by a Mr. Permee, while the NHLR says Porter bought the land; these may or may not be the same parcel. The record's rental field is null; the NHLR rental note is undated.
